english: Let $D$ be the set of all real numbers $x$ for which $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{[x]}{2}\right)-\cos^{-1}\left(x-[x]\right)$ is defined, where $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$ and the inverse trigonometric functions take their principal values. Let $f:D\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{[x]}{2}\right)-\cos^{-1}\left(x-[x]\right)$. If the range of $f$ is the interval $[\alpha,\beta)$, then the value of $\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $D$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{[x]}{2}\right)-\cos^{-1}\left(x-[x]\right)$ परिभाषित है, जहाँ $[t]$, $t$ से कम या उसके बराबर महत्तम पूर्णांक को दर्शाता है तथा प्रतिलोम त्रिकोणमितीय फलन अपने मुख्य मान लेते हैं। माना कि $f:D\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{[x]}{2}\right)-\cos^{-1}\left(x-[x]\right)$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। यदि $f$ का परिसर अन्तराल $[\alpha,\beta)$ है, तो $\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: For $[x]=n$, $\{x\}$ takes every value in $[0,1)$, so $\cos^{-1}\{x\}$ takes every value in $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$
Hence on $[n,n+1)$ the values of $f$ fill $\left[s_{n}-\dfrac{\pi}{2},s_{n}\right)$ with $s_{n}=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{n}{2}=-\dfrac{\pi}{2},-\dfrac{\pi}{6},0,\dfrac{\pi}{6},\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
solution_full: Domain. $x-[x]=\{x\}$, the fractional part, lies in $[0,1)\subset[-1,1]$, so $\cos^{-1}(x-[x])$ is defined for every real $x$. For $\sin^{-1}\dfrac{[x]}{2}$ we need $-1\le\dfrac{[x]}{2}\le1$, i.e. the integer $[x]\in\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$, i.e. $-2\le x<3$. So $D=[-2,3)$.

Fix $n=[x]\in\{-2,\ldots,2\}$. As $x$ runs over $[n,n+1)$, $t=x-n$ runs over all of $[0,1)$. Since $\cos^{-1}$ is decreasing on $[0,1]$ with $\cos^{-1}0=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\cos^{-1}1=0$, $\cos^{-1}t$ runs over $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ (the value $0$ is excluded because $t=1$ is excluded).

So on $[n,n+1)$, $f=s_{n}-\cos^{-1}t$ takes exactly the values in $\left[s_{n}-\dfrac{\pi}{2},s_{n}\right)$, where $s_{n}=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{n}{2}$: $s_{-2}=-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $s_{-1}=-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $s_{0}=0$, $s_{1}=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $s_{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

The five pieces are $\left[-\pi,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\left[-\dfrac{2\pi}{3},-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$, $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)$, $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{3},\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$, $\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Each piece starts before the previous one ends (for example $-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}<-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$), so there is no gap and the union is $\left[-\pi,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

The least value $-\pi$ is attained at $x=-2$: $\sin^{-1}(-1)-\cos^{-1}0=-\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{\pi}{2}=-\pi$. The value $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ would need $\cos^{-1}t=0$, i.e. $t=1$, which is impossible, so it is not attained. Thus $\alpha=-\pi$ and $\beta=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
originality_note: New: the range is assembled as a union of five shifted copies of (0, pi/2], one per value of [x], with the fractional part sweeping [0,1) on each unit interval; the endpoint behaviour of {x} decides which end is closed (way 5). Closest known: range of sin^-1[x] + cos^-1[x] type questions, which give a finite set. Different because: the greatest integer and fractional part act together, giving an interval range with one open end.

concept_use.Domain and range of inverse trigonometri: Domain of sin^-1 forces [x] in {-2,...,2} so D = [-2,3); the range of cos^-1 on [0,1) is (0,pi/2], and the union of ranges gives [-pi, pi/2).
concept_use.Standard functions and their graphs (pol: The greatest integer function fixes s_n on each unit interval and the fractional part x-[x] sweeps [0,1), never reaching 1.
